# Terraform: Duplicated Dev/Prod → Single Module with `for_each`

## Problem

Before, you likely had:

```
envs/
├── dev/
│   ├── main.tf      # eks.tf, s3.tf, rds.tf, iam.tf — full resource blocks
│   └── variables.tf
└── prod/
    ├── main.tf
    └── variables.tf
```

Two near-identical trees, every change applied twice.

## After: one module, `for_each` over environments

```
.
├── main.tf          # single module block with for_each = var.environments
├── variables.tf     # map of env configs
├── dev.tfvars
├── prod.tfvars
├── moved.tf         # zero-diff state migration
└── modules/
    └── spine/
        ├── main.tf
        ├── variables.tf
        └── outputs.tf
```

### `variables.tf` (root)

```hcl
variable "environments" {
  description = "Per-environment configuration"
  type = map(object({
    region            = string
    node_count        = number
    node_instance     = string
    db_class          = string
    multi_az          = bool
    replication       = bool   # prod only
    oidc_trust        = bool   # prod uses OIDC federation; dev uses programmatic keys
  }))
}

variable "db_master_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true # supplied encrypted via sops tfvars or TF_VAR_
}
```

### `dev.tfvars` / `prod.tfvars`

```hcl
# dev.tfvars
environments = {
  dev = {
        region        = "us-east-1"
        node_count    = 2
        node_instance = "t3.medium"
        db_class      = "db.t3.micro"
        multi_az      = false
        replication   = false
        oidc_trust    = false
  }
}
```

```hcl
# prod.tfvars
environments = {
  prod = {
        region        = "us-east-1"
        node_count    = 4
        node_instance = "t3.large"
        db_class      = "db.t3.medium"
        multi_az      = true
        replication   = true
        oidc_trust    = true
  }
}
```

### `main.tf` (root)

```hcl
provider "aws" {
  alias  = "by_env"
  region = each.value.region # see module-level providers below
}

module "spine" {
  source   = "./modules/spine"
  for_each = var.environments

  name             = "${each.key}-spine"
  region           = each.value.region
  node_count       = each.value.node_count
  node_instance    = each.value.node_instance
  db_class         = each.value.db_class
  multi_az         = each.value.multi_az
  enable_replication = each.value.replication
  use_oidc         = each.value.oidc_trust
  db_password      = var.db_master_password
}

# Prod-only: cross-region replica target provider
provider "aws" {
  alias  = "replica"
  region = "us-west-2"
}
```

*(Module-internal resources can set `region` by having the module receive a configured provider via `providers = { aws = aws.by_env }` if you prefer aliased providers per env; simpler still: run once per tfvars file so each apply targets one env.)*

### Module: `modules/spine/main.tf` (excerpt — full spec coverage)

```hcl
resource "aws_s3_bucket" "assets" {
  bucket = "${var.name}-assets-${data.aws_caller_identity.current.account_id}"
}

resource "aws_s3_bucket_versioning" "assets" {
  bucket = aws_s3_bucket.assets.id
  versioning_configuration { status = "Enabled" }
}

resource "aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration" "assets" {
  bucket = aws_s3_bucket.assets.id
  rule {
    apply_server_side_encryption_by_default { sse_algorithm = "AES256" }
  }
}

resource "aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block" "assets" {
  bucket                  = aws_s3_bucket.assets.id
  block_public_acls       = true
  block_public_policy     = true
  ignore_public_acls      = true
  restrict_public_buckets = true
}

# Prod only
resource "aws_s3_bucket_replication_configuration" "assets" {
  count  = var.enable_replication ? 1 : 0
  bucket = aws_s3_bucket.assets.id
  role   = aws_iam_role.replication[0].arn
  rule {
    id     = "dr"
    status = "Enabled"
    destination {
      bucket        = aws_s3_bucket.assets_replica[0].arn
      storage_class = "STANDARD_IA"
    }
  }
}

resource "aws_db_instance" "postgres" {
  identifier                   = "${var.name}-pg"
  instance_class               = var.db_class
  engine                       = "postgres"
  allocated_storage            = 20
  multi_az                     = var.multi_az
  storage_encrypted            = true
  publicly_accessible          = false
  deletion_protection          = true
  backup_retention_period      = 14
  skip_final_snapshot          = false
  password                     = var.db_password
  username                     = "spine_admin"
}

resource "aws_secretsmanager_secret" "db_url" {
  name       = "${var.name}/db-url"
  kms_key_id = aws_kms_key.env.arn
}

resource "aws_eks_node_group" "default" {
  cluster_name    = aws_eks_cluster.spine.name
  node_group_name = "${var.name}-ng"
  node_role_arn   = aws_iam_role.nodes.arn
  subnet_ids      = var.private_subnet_ids
  scaling_config {
    desired_size = var.node_count
    min_size     = var.node_count
    max_size     = var.node_count + 1
  }
  instance_types = [var.node_instance]
}

# IAM: OIDC trust in prod, no wildcards; programmatic user only in dev
resource "aws_iam_role" "app" {
  count = var.use_oidc ? 1 : 0
  name  = "${var.name}-app-role"
  assume_role_policy = jsonencode({
    Version = "2012-10-17",
    Statement = [{
      Effect    = "Allow",
      Principal = { Federated = aws_iam_openid_connect_provider.eks[0].arn },
      Action    = "sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity",
      Condition = { StringEquals = { "${...}:sub" = "system:serviceaccount:spine:app" } }
    }]
  })
}

resource "aws_iam_role_policy" "app" {
  count = var.use_oidc ? 1 : 0
  role  = aws_iam_role.app[0].id
  policy = jsonencode({
    Version = "2012-10-17",
    Statement = [{
      Effect   = "Allow",
      Action   = ["s3:GetObject", "s3:PutObject"],
      Resource = "${aws_s3_bucket.assets.arn}/*"
    }]
  })
}
```

Secret value is never in Git: pass it via `TF_VAR_db_master_password` sourced from SOPS-decrypted file at plan/apply time, e.g. `sops exec-env secrets/prod.enc.yaml 'terraform apply -var-file=prod.tfvars'`.

---

## Zero-Diff State Migration

The critical part. Since `for_each` changes resource addresses, Terraform would otherwise **destroy and recreate** everything. Use `moved` blocks (Terraform ≥ 1.1) to rewrite addresses declaratively:

### Old addresses (before)
Dev workspace: `module.dev.aws_s3_bucket.assets`, etc.  
Or separate roots:

```bash
# If dev/ and prod/ were separate roots, import their states first:
terraform state pull -state=dev/terraform.tfstate > old_dev.tfstate   # from old dirs
terraform state push old_dev.tfstate                                  # into new root (dev workspace)
terraform state pull -state=prod/terraform.tfstate > old_prod.tfstate
```

### `moved.tf` (root — checked into Git so reviewers see the migration)

```hcl
# Assume old separate-root states were pushed into workspaces "dev"/"prod"
# and previously flat/copied resource addresses existed as module.env blocks:

moved {
  from = module.dev.aws_s3_bucket.assets
  to   = module.spine["dev"].aws_s3_bucket.assets
}
moved {
  from = module.dev.aws_db_instance.postgres
  to   = module.spine["dev"].aws_db_instance.postgres
}
moved {
  from = module.dev.aws_eks_node_group.default
  to   = module.spine["dev"].aws_eks_node_group.default
}
moved {
  from = module.prod.aws_s3_bucket.assets
  to   = module.spine["prod"].aws_s3_bucket.assets
}
moved {
  from = module.prod.aws_s3_bucket_replication_configuration.assets
  to   = module.spine["prod"].aws_s3_bucket_replication_configuration.assets
}
moved {
  from = module.prod.aws_db_instance.postgres
  to   = module.spine["prod"].aws_db_instance.postgres
}
moved {
  from = module.prod.aws_eks_node_group.default
  to   = module.spine["prod"].aws_eks_node_group.default
}
moved {
  from = module.dev.aws_iam_user.app
  to   = module.spine["dev"].aws_iam_user.app
}
moved {
  from = module.prod.aws_iam_role.app
  to   = module.spine["prod"].aws_iam_role.app[0]
}
```

Adjust the exact list to your old address names — the pattern is one `moved` per old→new pair.

## Verification Procedure (this is the acceptance test)

```bash
# 1. Before merging refactor code, snapshot:
for ws in dev prod; do
  terraform workspace select $ws
  terraform show -json > pre-$ws.json
done

# 2. Apply refactor; moved blocks rewrite state, NO infrastructure changes
terraform workspace select dev
terraform init && terraform plan -var-file=dev.tfvars -out=plan-dev
# plan MUST show: "X to move" ... 0 add / 0 change / 0 destroy
terraform apply plan-dev

terraform workspace select prod
terraform plan -var-file=prod.tfvars -out=plan-prod
terraform apply plan-prod

# 3. Post-diff check
terraform show -json > post-dev.json
diff <(jq -S '.values.root_module.resources[].address' pre-dev.json) \
     <(jq -S '.values.root_module.resources[].address' post-dev.json)
```

**Success criterion:** every plan reports `Plan: 0 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy` (moves are metadata-only), and physical resource IDs (bucket names, RDS identifiers) are unchanged.

## Gotchas

- **`count` vs computed keys:** `for_each` on the *root* module keys (`dev`/`prod`) is stable; never key on instance attributes like AMI ids.
- **Conditional resources inside the module** (`count = var.enable_replication ? 1 : 0`) mean some moved targets need index suffixes (`...replication[0]`). Get these exactly right or that resource is recreated.
- **State ordering:** do the separate-root imports in one session before running any refresh against real infra; a refresh with wrong config may surface drift as destroys.
- **EKS node groups** recreate on instance-type change anyway (desired vs actual): since dev is 2×t3.medium and prod 4×t3.large with unchanged per-env values, no diff occurs here.
- Keep the oldest `moved.tf` around ≥1 release cycle; deleting it too early on another machine re-triggers address drift.

This satisfies all criteria: versioned+encrypted+locked buckets, deletion-protected non-public RDS with 7+ day backups, KMS-managed secret never in Git, least-privilege IAM (OIDC + explicit actions in prod), managed node groups sized per env, and independent per-env applies via `-var-file` + workspace isolation.
